title: Automated testing with pytest
why_md: **Highest-priority gap.** None of your 9 personal projects has a test, and the work harness (`lambda_test.py`) is manual. Every backend interview at your level will ask how you test, and tests are what let you refactor 150+ processors safely.
prerequisites_md: Python functions, modules, exceptions (you have these).

steps.title: Study: pytest essentials (fixtures, parametrize, monkeypatch)
Write 10 parametrized tests for a pure function (e.g. parse_target from your downloader)
Test a FastAPI app with TestClient (status codes + validation errors)
Mock an external call (requests / boto3) with monkeypatch or unittest.mock
Measure coverage with pytest-cov and read the report

exercises_md:
- Python practice exercises: run them, then write your own tests for the same functions.
- Read `backend/tests/` in this platform — every revision-engine rule is unit-tested.
mini_projects_md: Add a `tests/` folder to **InstaPostDownloader**: test `parse_target`, `normalize_username`, `_safe_under` (path traversal!) and the `/api/download` 400 path.
outcome_md: You can explain unit vs integration tests, write fixtures and mocks, and show a tested personal project on GitHub.

title: SQL depth: verify and deepen
why_md: You write SQL daily, but the evidence only shows upserts. Interviews for Python/PostgreSQL roles almost always include joins, GROUP BY/HAVING, CTEs and window functions. Prove these to yourself with the challenges — skip what you already ace.

steps.title: Joins incl. anti-joins (orders without settlements)
GROUP BY, HAVING, conditional aggregation
Subqueries: IN, EXISTS, correlated
CTEs and recursive CTEs
Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, running totals
NULL semantics, COALESCE, NULLIF
Solve every easy + medium SQL challenge in Practice

mini_projects_md: Write the reconciliation query you'd use at work — orders vs settlements with mismatch reasons — using CTEs and window functions.
outcome_md: Comfortably solve medium SQL interview questions without looking anything up.

title: PostgreSQL performance: indexes, EXPLAIN, locking
why_md: Your resume claims a **40% reconciliation speed-up**. Interviewers will dig: which plan changed, which index, why batching helped. This track turns the claim into a story you can defend.

steps.title: Index types: B-tree, composite order, partial, covering
Read EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) output
Isolation levels, deadlocks, retry strategies
Upserts in depth (DO NOTHING vs DO UPDATE, EXCLUDED)
psycopg2 batching: execute_batch vs execute_values vs COPY
Write a 1-page note: exactly how the 40% speed-up was achieved

exercises_md: SQL challenges tagged indexing / query-optimization; interview scenario questions on slow queries.
mini_projects_md: Load 1M fake orders into a local Postgres (Docker), time a reconciliation query, add indexes, compare EXPLAIN plans before/after.
outcome_md: You can read a query plan, pick the right index, and explain your optimization work with numbers.

title: Python depth for interviews
why_md: You use Python every day, but interviews probe language internals: decorators, generators, context managers, mutability, typing. These also make your production code cleaner (e.g. a `@retry` decorator for deadlocks, a context manager for DB transactions).
prerequisites_md: None — skip any topic you can already explain.

steps.title: Data structures & comprehensions (complexities)
Functions: *args/**kwargs, closures, mutable defaults
Decorators (write a retry decorator)
Generators & iterators (stream a large CSV)
Context managers (transaction scope)
Exceptions & custom hierarchies
Classes, dataclasses
Type hints & typing

exercises_md: Python + debugging exercises in Coding Practice.
mini_projects_md: Refactor one of your CLI tools: generator-based file walking, a `@timed` decorator, a context manager for temp output.
outcome_md: Confidently answer 'how does X work under the hood' questions with code.

title: pandas: cleaning and performance
why_md: pandas is the core of your ingestion work. Going from 'it works' to 'it's fast and correct with messy data' (dtypes, vectorisation, chunking, memory) directly improves your day job.

steps.title: pandas essentials refresher
Cleaning, dtypes, vectorisation vs apply, chunked reads

exercises_md: Write timing comparisons: `apply` vs vectorised `np.where` on 1M rows.
mini_projects_md: Build a reusable `normalize_columns()` + schema check for marketplace reports, with tests.
outcome_md: Your processors are faster and you can explain why.

title: REST API design
why_md: Most of your API experience is **consuming** APIs. Designing them well (resources, status codes, pagination, idempotency, versioning, error format) is expected of a backend developer and is the bridge to building your own services.
prerequisites_md: HTTP basics, FastAPI basics (from your downloaders).

steps.title: REST design principles
FastAPI properly: routers, Depends, response models
Retries, backoff, idempotency keys
Streaming progress: SSE vs WebSockets vs polling

exercises_md: Backend/scenario exercises: pagination design, webhook receiver, rate-limit handling.
mini_projects_md: Part of the capstone API project.
outcome_md: You can design a clean, consistent API and justify every choice.

title: AWS beyond the basics
why_md: You use Lambda, ECS, S3 and DynamoDB at work. Strengthen the *why*: when Lambda vs ECS, concurrency limits, timeouts, presigned URL security, DynamoDB key design.

steps.title: Lambda: cold starts, layers, timeouts, concurrency
S3 presigned URLs & security
ECS / Fargate: tasks, services, run_task
DynamoDB key design, Query vs Scan

exercises_md: Scenario: 'Lambda times out on a 200MB XLSX'.
mini_projects_md: Diagram your work's ingestion architecture and annotate each AWS choice with its trade-off.
outcome_md: You can justify every AWS service choice in your work project.

title: Async & concurrency in Python
why_md: You've used `asyncio.to_thread`, executors and `threading.Event` in personal apps. Solidify the model (event loop, GIL, when threads vs processes vs async) — it's a frequent interview topic and FastAPI relies on it.

steps.title: asyncio: event loop, tasks, to_thread
Threads, the GIL, threading.Event

exercises_md: Explain why your downloader routes don't block while downloads run.
mini_projects_md: Fetch 50 URLs with `httpx.AsyncClient` + a semaphore limit; compare with a ThreadPoolExecutor version.
outcome_md: You can pick the right concurrency model and explain why.

title: JavaScript & TypeScript without AI help
why_md: Your React/Next/TS apps were AI-assisted. If you want frontend in your toolkit, build fluency by writing small pieces yourself. Optional for a backend role — prioritise after testing, SQL and auth.
prerequisites_md: Basic JS (you have it from Bol Hindi).

steps.title: Promises, async/await, the event loop
React hooks: useState, useEffect, custom hooks
Solve the JavaScript exercises without AI

mini_projects_md: Add one small page to this platform's frontend yourself.
outcome_md: You can read and modify React/TS code confidently.

title: Authentication & web security
why_md: No auth implementation exists in any of your projects. Login, password hashing, JWT/OAuth2 and basic OWASP knowledge are standard backend expectations.

steps.title: JWT & OAuth2 password flow, hashing
OWASP basics: injection, broken auth, secrets
Implement signup/login with hashed passwords and JWT in FastAPI
Add role-based authorization to one endpoint

exercises_md: Interview questions on auth; scenario: idempotent payment webhook with signature verification.
mini_projects_md: Part of the capstone API project.
outcome_md: You can implement and explain token-based auth securely.

title: SQLAlchemy 2.0 & Alembic migrations
why_md: You've only used raw SQL. Most Python teams use SQLAlchemy and Alembic. With your SQL strength you'll pick it up quickly — and you can read this platform's `models.py` as a real example.

steps.title: SQLAlchemy 2.0: engine, Session, Mapped models, select()
Read backend/app/models.py and one router of this platform
Add Alembic to a toy project; create and roll back a migration
Spot and fix an N+1 query with selectinload

exercises_md: Rewrite two of your SQL challenge answers using SQLAlchemy Core.
mini_projects_md: Part of the capstone API project.
outcome_md: You can work in an ORM codebase and manage schema changes safely.

title: Docker for your own projects + CI
why_md: Docker is on your resume but in none of your personal projects; CI/CD isn't anywhere. A public repo with a Dockerfile and a green GitHub Actions badge is strong evidence.

steps.title: Dockerfiles, layers, multi-stage builds
GitHub Actions: lint + test on every push
Git workflow refresher: branches, rebase, PRs
Put one personal project on GitHub with CI

mini_projects_md: Dockerize YoutubePlaylistDownloader (ffmpeg included) and add CI running pytest.
outcome_md: Every new project ships with a Dockerfile, tests and CI.

title: System design fundamentals
why_md: You've built a real multi-tenant ingestion system — great material. Learn the vocabulary and structure (requirements → estimates → components → trade-offs) to present it, and to answer unseen design questions.

steps.title: Normalisation and data modelling trade-offs
Caching strategies
Message queues & idempotent consumers
Practise 5 system-design interview questions out loud
Write a design doc of your ingestion service as if proposing it today

mini_projects_md: Design doc for 'ingestion v2' with a queue, DLQ and per-report schema registry.
outcome_md: You can lead a 45-minute design discussion with clear trade-offs.

title: Redis caching & background job queues
why_md: Industry-standard next step after cron/Lambda-triggered pipelines: Redis for caching/rate limiting and a queue (SQS, Celery, RQ) for retries and back-pressure.

steps.title: Caching patterns: cache-aside, TTL, invalidation
Queues: at-least-once delivery, DLQ, idempotency
Run Redis in Docker and cache an expensive endpoint
Move a long-running job to a worker queue

mini_projects_md: Replace the in-memory job dict in your downloader with Redis + RQ/Celery so jobs survive restarts.
outcome_md: You can add caching and background processing to any API.

title: Logging & observability
why_md: Your personal code uses print/console.warn. Structured logs, correlation IDs (e.g. upload UUID), metrics and alarms are how production issues get found fast.

steps.title: Python logging module + JSON structured logs
Correlation IDs across a request/job
CloudWatch Logs Insights queries, metrics and alarms

mini_projects_md: Add structured logging with job IDs to one downloader.
outcome_md: You can debug production from logs alone.

title: Capstone: production-style REST API on GitHub
why_md: Your resume has a commented-out placeholder: *'add your FastAPI project here once it is on GitHub'*. Your work code is private — this public project is proof of the skills from the tracks above, all in one place.
prerequisites_md: Testing, SQLAlchemy, authentication, Docker/CI tracks (can be done in parallel).

steps.title: Pick a domain you know (e.g. order + settlement reconciliation API)
FastAPI + PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic
JWT auth with roles
Pagination, filtering, idempotency keys, consistent error format
pytest suite ≥ 80% coverage
Dockerfile + docker-compose (api + postgres)
GitHub Actions CI + README with architecture diagram
Add it to the resume Projects section

outcome_md: A public, tested, documented API project that backs up every line of your resume.

title: Mini ingestion pipeline (public re-creation of your work patterns)
why_md: Re-create the *patterns* (not the code) of your work service publicly: registry dispatcher, column validation, upserts, status tracking — this time with tests. Great for interviews and for revising your own design decisions.

steps.title: Registry/dispatcher with lazy imports
read_and_validate for CSV/XLSX with clear missing-column errors
Upserts with ON CONFLICT into Postgres
Upload status table + tests with fixture files

mini_projects_md: This is the project. Use fake marketplace data only.
outcome_md: You can demo and discuss your core work architecture with real, public code.
